# Upstream

Based on the exact crates.io tao 0.35.3 package (SHA-256 `d1c93047acf68669466a34690ac58cca7010bd1b201e1ec86f1fd0a75d3dd4a9`, packaged from tauri-apps/tao commit `5a14e624c81b7a799728129417e9218be25f17d9`). The normalized Cargo.toml, `src`, README and licenses are the package contents; the upstream examples are not carried.

The fullscreen and mouse-capture patches below are in `src/platform_impl/windows/event_loop.rs`. The session-termination patch additionally touches `src/event_loop.rs`, the Windows runner, and the macOS app delegate/state; `Cargo.toml` enables the Windows shutdown APIs.

`WM_NCCALCSIZE`: a fullscreen window keeps its whole window rectangle as its client area. Upstream clamps a maximized undecorated window to the monitor work area even while it is fullscreen, which leaves a taskbar-sized strip unpainted and pillarboxes fullscreen video. This is tauri-apps/tao#1353, released as tao 0.37.2; that part can go when `vendor/wry` and `vendor/tauri-runtime-wry` move to a tao that contains it.

Mouse capture: a window gives up the capture it took for a button press once no button holds it (`WM_MOUSEMOVE` without a button, `WM_KILLFOCUS` with none down), and whenever Windows cancels modes (`WM_CANCELMODE`, `WM_ACTIVATEAPP` losing activation). Upstream releases only when its own button-up arrives; a press whose release lands on another window left the browser window holding the capture, and Windows sends no `WM_SETCURSOR` to anyone while it is held, so the pointer kept whatever shape it last had. Not yet upstream, so this directory stays until tao carries an equivalent.

System termination: a host-installed handler enters the application's existing shutdown coordinator once, with a caller-owned budget and localized Windows blocking reason. Windows `WM_QUERYENDSESSION` starts it; `WM_ENDSESSION(TRUE)` pumps the UI apartment until accepted event-loop exit or the deadline, then delivers terminal destruction. Cancelled Windows session termination removes the blocking reason; a shutdown already started remains terminal. macOS `applicationShouldTerminate:` returns `NSTerminateLater`, preserves main-queue cleanup, and replies after terminal cleanup, with a deadline that stops the loop unsuccessfully. Reentrant `applicationWillTerminate:` cannot deliver destruction twice. Hosts without a handler keep upstream termination behavior. Keep this patch until upstream exposes equivalent deferred OS-session shutdown hooks. Unit/source tests do not replace sign-out/restart and Dock Quit qualification on devices.

GTK configure events: `src/platform_impl/linux/event_loop.rs` reports `Moved`/`Resized` only for the toplevel's own GdkWindow. GTK 3 on Wayland gives a `GtkPopover` its own surface, whose configure event reached the toplevel's handler; upstream reported the popover's size as the window's, so the browser laid its tab out for a popover-sized window while one was open. Not yet upstream.
